melbourne-1.name: Flinders Street Station
melbourne-1.bio: Victoria's busiest railway station, an Edwardian Baroque building from 1909 opposite Federation Square.

melbourne-2.name: Federation Square
melbourne-2.bio: Melbourne's main meeting place, opposite Flinders Street Station, with cultural venues around the square.

melbourne-3.name: Queen Victoria Market
melbourne-3.bio: Open-air market opened in 1878, covering over seven hectares and billed as the Southern Hemisphere's largest.

melbourne-4.name: NGV International
melbourne-4.bio: Free-entry gallery at 180 St Kilda Road with art from Europe, Asia, America and Oceania.

melbourne-5.name: Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria
melbourne-5.bio: A 38-hectare garden founded in 1846 on the Yarra, with lakes, lawns and almost 50,000 plants, free to enter.

melbourne-6.name: Melbourne Cricket Ground
melbourne-6.bio: Cricket ground with 75-minute behind-the-scenes tours from Gate 3 on select event days, and a sports museum.

melbourne-7.name: Royal Exhibition Building
melbourne-7.bio: UNESCO-listed hall built for the 1880 exhibition, where Australia's first Parliament opened in 1901, visited on tours.

melbourne-8.name: Melbourne Museum
melbourne-8.bio: Natural and cultural history museum in Carlton Gardens with the Bunjilaka Aboriginal Cultural Centre and an IMAX cinema.

melbourne-9.name: Hosier Lane
melbourne-9.bio: A colourful street-art lane across from Federation Square, free to walk through in Melbourne.

melbourne-10.name: St Kilda Beach
melbourne-10.bio: Sandy bay beach on Port Phillip and a popular stop on the St Kilda foreshore.

melbourne-11.name: Luna Park Melbourne
melbourne-11.bio: St Kilda amusement park from 1912 with the Mr Moon entrance and the world's oldest continuously operating roller coaster.

melbourne-12.name: Eureka Tower
melbourne-12.bio: Melbourne Skydeck, the observation deck atop Eureka Tower, has a glass cube, The Edge, that juts 3 metres out.

melbourne-13.name: Shrine of Remembrance
melbourne-13.bio: 1934 classical memorial with exhibition galleries under it, open to visitors daily in Melbourne.

melbourne-14.name: Old Melbourne Gaol
melbourne-14.bio: Victoria's oldest prison, now a museum with day and night tours and cells devoted to the gaol's women and children.

melbourne-15.name: State Library of Victoria
melbourne-15.bio: Domed reading room dating from 1854, open to the public with exhibitions and the La Trobe Reading Room.

melbourne-16.name: Melbourne Zoo
melbourne-16.bio: Zoos Victoria's zoo in Royal Park, open daily, home to critically endangered western lowland gorillas.

melbourne-17.name: Werribee Open Range Zoo
melbourne-17.bio: A wildlife safari in Melbourne's west, with a free safari bus and nine Asian elephants on the Elephant Trail.

melbourne-18.name: Heide Museum of Modern Art
melbourne-18.bio: Art museum and sculpture park on the Yarra in Bulleen, where the gardens and sculpture park are free to enter.

melbourne-19.name: Brighton Beach and Bathing Boxes
melbourne-19.bio: Dendy Street Beach in Brighton, lined with 96 heritage-listed bathing boxes along 500 m of sand, mostly built 1907 to 1933.

melbourne-20.name: Williamstown
melbourne-20.bio: Bayside waterfront town with Nelson Place, beaches and the Williamstown Botanic Gardens.

melbourne-21.name: Immigration Museum
melbourne-21.bio: Museum in the Old Customs House at 400 Flinders Street exploring migration to Victoria through its galleries.

melbourne-22.name: Australian Centre for the Moving Image
melbourne-22.bio: Australia's national museum of screen culture at Federation Square, with a free exhibition on film, TV and games.

melbourne-23.name: Arts Centre Melbourne
melbourne-23.bio: Performing arts precinct on St Kilda Road with Hamer Hall, theatres and the landmark spire, designed by Roy Grounds.

melbourne-24.name: St Patrick's Cathedral
melbourne-24.bio: Bluestone Gothic Revival cathedral by William Wardell, built from 1858 to 1939 on Gisborne Street in East Melbourne.

melbourne-25.name: St Paul's Cathedral
melbourne-25.bio: Anglican cathedral on Flinders Street opposite Federation Square, open daily with free admission.

melbourne-26.name: Fitzroy Gardens
melbourne-26.bio: Heritage-listed 26-hectare gardens in East Melbourne, lined with elms and holding a conservatory and Cooks' Cottage.

melbourne-27.name: Cooks' Cottage
melbourne-27.bio: Captain Cook's parents' 1755 Yorkshire cottage, moved to Melbourne in 1934 and rebuilt in Fitzroy Gardens.

melbourne-28.name: Parliament House of Victoria
melbourne-28.bio: Parliament House, opened in 1856, offers free public and architecture tours except when Parliament is sitting.

melbourne-29.name: Carlton Gardens
melbourne-29.bio: 26-hectare Victorian gardens around the Royal Exhibition Building and Melbourne Museum, part of a World Heritage site.

melbourne-30.name: Melbourne Park
melbourne-30.bio: Home of the Australian Open since 1988, where Rod Laver Arena seats about 15,000 and also hosts concerts.

melbourne-31.name: Albert Park and Lake
melbourne-31.bio: Urban park around an artificial lake 3 km south of the CBD, with a 4.7 km walking track and skyline views.

melbourne-32.name: Block Arcade
melbourne-32.bio: Mosaic-floored 1890s arcade between Collins and Elizabeth Streets, home to the original Hopetoun Tea Rooms.

melbourne-33.name: Royal Arcade
melbourne-33.bio: Australia's oldest surviving arcade, opened in 1870, where Gog and Magog strike Gaunt's clock bells each hour.

melbourne-34.name: ACDC Lane
melbourne-34.bio: Alley renamed in 2004 after the rock band, with a sign that fans photograph.

melbourne-35.name: Chinatown
melbourne-35.bio: Little Bourke Street Chinatown with restaurants and arches in Melbourne.

melbourne-36.name: Lygon Street
melbourne-36.bio: Italian dining strip running through Carlton, a street to walk for its restaurants.

melbourne-37.name: Brunswick Street
melbourne-37.bio: Brunswick Street is a bohemian shopping and dining strip in Fitzroy, Melbourne.

melbourne-38.name: Chapel Street
melbourne-38.bio: Shopping and nightlife strip running through Prahran and South Yarra.

melbourne-39.name: Acland Street
melbourne-39.bio: St Kilda street of restaurants and European-style cake shops near the beach, long tied to Melbourne's Jewish community.

melbourne-40.name: St Kilda Pier
melbourne-40.bio: A 300 m pier and 750 m breakwater in Port Phillip Bay, with a historic kiosk and a little penguin colony.

melbourne-41.name: Rippon Lea Estate
melbourne-41.bio: Heritage mansion and 14 acres of gardens in Elsternwick, with a lake and fernery, the house by guided tour only.

melbourne-42.name: Werribee Park
melbourne-42.bio: Estate with the heritage Werribee Mansion, an ornamental lake and a State Rose Garden of about 5000 roses.

melbourne-43.name: Melbourne Aquarium
melbourne-43.bio: Yarra-side aquarium with over 10,000 animals, including king and gentoo penguins, sharks and a saltwater crocodile.

melbourne-45.name: Ian Potter Centre
melbourne-45.bio: The National Gallery of Victoria's home of Australian art at Federation Square, free apart from special exhibitions.

melbourne-46.name: Old Treasury Building
melbourne-46.bio: Free, self-guided museum in the 1858 Old Treasury Building on Spring Street, with ticketed guided tours.

melbourne-47.name: Polly Woodside
melbourne-47.bio: An 1885 iron-hulled barque run by the National Trust as a maritime museum at South Wharf, open on set days.

melbourne-48.name: Chinese Museum
melbourne-48.bio: Museum of Chinese Australian history in Chinatown, with adult tickets bought at the door.

melbourne-49.name: Koorie Heritage Trust
melbourne-49.bio: Cultural centre for Aboriginal Victoria with free entry, running the Birrarung Wilam and Scar Tree walking tours.

melbourne-50.name: Como House
melbourne-50.bio: An 1847 National Trust house and garden estate in South Yarra, with free gardens and house entry by guided tour only.

melbourne-51.name: Prahran Market
melbourne-51.bio: A permanent food market in Prahran that trades from Tuesday to Saturday.

melbourne-52.name: Footscray Market
melbourne-52.bio: Indoor market on Hopkins Street in Footscray with butchers, seafood, poultry, grocery and takeaway traders.

melbourne-53.name: Dandenong Market
melbourne-53.bio: Market in Dandenong since 1866, with over 200 traders from about 150 nationalities, open Friday to Sunday.

melbourne-54.name: Capital City Trail
melbourne-54.bio: A 29 km sealed shared path looping Melbourne's centre and inner suburbs, easy riding from Princes Bridge.

melbourne-55.name: Yarra Bend Park
melbourne-55.bio: Melbourne's largest natural bushland park on the Yarra, with a flying-fox viewing platform and Dights Falls.

melbourne-56.name: Warrandyte State Park
melbourne-56.bio: Yarra River state park 24 km from the city, with kangaroos often seen at Pound Bend and gold-mining relics.

melbourne-57.name: Organ Pipes National Park
melbourne-57.bio: Basalt columns like organ pipes hang over Jacksons Creek, reached by a short, steep path from the car park.

melbourne-58.name: Maranoa Botanic Gardens
melbourne-58.bio: Council-run botanic garden in Balwyn with more than 4,000 native plants along winding paths.

melbourne-59.name: CERES Community Environment Park
melbourne-59.bio: Free community environment park in Brunswick East with a farm, nursery and cafe, plus a Saturday market.

melbourne-60.name: Jewish Museum of Australia
melbourne-60.bio: Jewish heritage and culture museum on Alma Road in St Kilda, closed on Mondays and Saturdays.

melbourne-61.name: Melbourne Holocaust Museum
melbourne-61.bio: Holocaust museum and education centre in Elsternwick with the Everybody Had a Name exhibition and a VR experience.

melbourne-62.name: Scienceworks
melbourne-62.bio: Museums Victoria science and technology museum at Spotswood on the Maribyrnong foreshore.

melbourne-63.name: RAAF Museum
melbourne-63.bio: Air Force museum on RAAF Base Point Cook, where booking is essential and photo ID is required over 16.

melbourne-64.name: Moorabbin Air Museum
melbourne-64.bio: Volunteer-run aviation museum at Moorabbin Airport, founded 1962, with the oldest surviving CAC Wirraway.

melbourne-65.name: Grainger Museum
melbourne-65.bio: Museum of composer Percy Grainger's life and music at the University of Melbourne, opened in 1938.

melbourne-66.name: Potter Museum of Art
melbourne-66.bio: Free university art museum on Swanston Street in Parkville, reopened in 2025 with changing exhibitions.

melbourne-67.name: Victoria Police Museum
melbourne-67.bio: Free police museum in Docklands with Australia's largest Kelly Gang armour collection, open Tuesday to Thursday.

melbourne-68.name: Altona Beach
melbourne-68.bio: Long bayside beach at Altona with a coastal park, in Melbourne.

melbourne-69.name: Elwood Beach
melbourne-69.bio: Bayside beach in Elwood on Port Phillip, named by a travel guide as a place to stop.

melbourne-70.name: Ramsay Street
melbourne-70.bio: Ramsay Street set of the television show Neighbours, visited by fans in Melbourne.

royal-botanic-gardens-cranbourne.name: Royal Botanic Gardens Cranbourne
royal-botanic-gardens-cranbourne.bio: Free botanic gardens centred on the Australian Garden, with the Red Sand Garden and a Eucalypt Walk.

mcclelland-gallery-and-sculpture-park.name: McClelland Gallery and Sculpture Park
mcclelland-gallery-and-sculpture-park.bio: Sculpture park and gallery in Langwarrin bushland, open Wednesday to Sunday, with a cafe and design store.
